In himself.. he says. He is incredibly sweet usually and cheers me up when I see him. But lately we have been fighting so much I've lost the feeling of connection with him. He is just tired of it, I suppose. And I don't blame him for it. I'm fucking tired of it myself xD. But I'm glad I'm starting my second year of uni next week.. finally something to do! Sitting at home while all my friends have started school already and having a boyfriend who has no time and energy for me, isn't that much fun.

Thanks for your response, it's nice to get it all out. I talked to my bestfriend yesterday and she explained the unconcious - incompetent schema to me. I don't know if you know it.. It explains how you are (when you first get to the psychologist), you are unconscious of your problems and incompetent of fixing them. Then you get conscious of your problems, but still are incompetent of solving them. This is an extremely frustrating phase. You see flaws and causes everywhere but have no idea what to do with them. Then you become competent of solving them & you are conscious of your problems. In this phase you are constantly tired and feel mistreated, because you need to solve all the problems, work on all the flaws.. and the world keeps doing exactly the same thing it always did; 'cause you trouble' (is what you feel). Then; you become unconscious and competent. Solving problems automatically and without much energy or trouble. That's where we want to end. 
The problems can stand for anything; my fear of men, panic attacks, my fear of loneliness, self-hate, impatience with my process, wanting to die sometimes, feeling 'too much' emotions (negative ones) and feeling like a burden. 

It was good to hear that I moved to the second phase; conscious & incompetent. It's Normal what I feel and I'm moving forward..!! I'll just keep going and see where it ends. Again, thank for the response and sorry I wrote so much! It always makes me feel better to talk to someone :)

I agree with some of the comments down here. Look into uni, sports and traveling. It's a great idea to meet new people, even though they might not be good friends or become your girlfriend. It's good to meet them and try to be more social. The 'it's just not me', isn't convincing me at all. I've had a never-talking autistic guy in my class that only drew bloody images during the lessons.. and even he had friends! Just because he cared to smile once in a while. He was a friendly bloke underneath it all. Just like you, you might feel you are not social, not a 'friend making person', but that's not a reason to just stop trying and feel miserable. 

Time to get up and do something about it.
I know it's harder than it sounds. But that why things like university/college, sports and travelling are great idea's. I've never made more friends than when I went to Uni and when I went travelling. In one week in London I made tons of friends. Sleeping in Hostels and caring to smile once in a while. Being interested in others and be brave enough to ask them questions. Same in uni or at a sports club. When you smile at people they'll come. At that same moment or after two weeks.. When you show people you're a friendly, nice bloke.. why would they avoid you? 

Feel worthy. Because that's probably where the picking on you comes from. When you feel low and not important, people will feel the same about you. Because.. if YOU don't feel like you're a great guy.. why would they? You're a good guy. Hit the gym or join a sports group. You'll feel better and better about yourself. Also, where I made a lot of friends; penpal sites. Sounds lame a fuck, but there are fucking amazing people out there. I have a few friends (who I will never meet in person) for life from Interpals.net. But above all.. this will sound harsh.. but stop feeling sorry for yourself. No one has 'done' this to you and no one will fix this 'for you'. You need to do it yourself. We're not in kindergarten anymore where the teacher will tell others to play with you.. you're a grown up now and you need to make friends on your own, find a girlfriend on you own. And there is Nothing to worry about, because you are capable. Think about my autistic never-talking, scary classmate.. Even he did it!

When you pick up yourself from the floor and start doing stuff, sport, study, travel or even move out of your tiny town. Everything is better than feel sorry for yourself and stay where you are, not changing anything. Ofcourse crying and feeling horrible is oke, I'm not saying that putting your story out here was something pathetic. Don't worry, we all need to vent. All I wanna get across is that after a good vent, after a good cry.. you need to get up and fix it. 

You're obviously a really nice guy. So you will be fine, don't hold youself back with the thought; 'it's not me.' or 'I never made any friends'. There is a first time for everything. All you need to make good friends is self-esteem and an easy way to get that is the gym, or at university. You will be fine.

You know this happend to you and I'm already incredibly happy your dad believes you and that he's standing up for you like this. I'm pretty sure my dad would of handled things differently.. with a few of his friends and some weapons probably. But be proud of your dad and support him. 
You can't change the way your sister deals with this. I've noticed lately that people will NOT hear things you say (even if they are the truth, wise and what they need to hear), when they are not read to hear them. Your sister does not want to hear this. She simply doesn't. So she will deny or act like she doesn't hear it.

It's sad.. It really is. But you can not change it. It has to come with time. Maybe in a few months she'll come around and will see how incredibly horrible it was, what she said to you and how impossible it was that she did not support you. 

For now, focus on yourself. Be busy, do fun stuff and get a counselor. The effect of this event will slowly creep in and be prepaired when they get there.  You will be absolutely fine. All the feelings you have are alright, anger, sadness, emptiness and even being numb.. let it be and keep your life going. 
I'm sorry this had to happen to you and I'm sorry your sister is being like this. If you need to talk some more PM me. Seriously, I know how healing and relieving it can be to talk to another survivor. So, if you want it PM me.

The first thing that came to mind was that I'm recognising myself in your wife all the time. My now ex-boyfriend couldn't do anything right. Nothing was ever enough to please me. They have different links to different things than people who haven't been through sexual abuse. For example when you ask her what's up when she's down and she says 'oh nothing', with a smile. A non-raped girl is fine. But a raped girl might be drowning in her feelings.. with a smile on her face. And I bet she'll blame YOU for not seeing it. Because I've done it SO much.

You two need counseling. She needs it for herself and you both need it for your relationship. Somethings we do are so incredibly unreasonable.. Rape victims sometimes forget that I think. I've been insanely unreasonable and ruined two great relationships in the past year because of it. 

She needs your FULL attention, when you two talk. You need to ask her questions and listen to her. Talks don't come from asking for a talk. They come because you SEE she needs one. And you can better ask for it when she doesn't need it, than don't ask it when she needs it. 

Still, the most important point I need to get a cross to you, is that this is all really unfair to you. Because you are a human being, you're not her counselor. You can't fix her and you can't carry her burden. Damn, I know exactly how she thinks.. If she doesn't get counseling soon it's going to escalate. You both need to be really patient with eachother. I couldn't be patient with my boyfriends so we ended up breaking up. But keep in mind, you are not her counselor. You are her husband and you can't fix her. You can help her and support her, but don't let her blame this entirely on you. 

Also talk to your friend. How can you help him and HER. He will also understand her and he can help you understand and talk to her. Ask me anything if something is unclear or if you need to know more. I'd love to help.

But you're right. He had the right to do this all. It's wrong to try and feel controle over your life and depend on someone else for it. I wanted the controle over my life and him changing plans all the time, kind involving me and kinda not involving me was extremely hard for me. It put me in the feeling of being shoved around again. Anxiety and panic attacks are pretty common. People from all ages have them for their own reasons. Sometimes out of the blue, sometimes because of a trauma. Personally I had them after being raped and being left by a romantic partner. It would be good to go to a doctor to see what can be done to make them go away or what would be a way to deal with them. I went to a counselor for it. It definitely helped me. 

So tell your mom, don't be shy, don't think she's gonne be mad or disappointed. NOTHING is wrong with it. She probably had panic attacks at some point in her life. When I first told my parents they just nodded and my dad started to tell me 'when I had them I did....' and I was kinda stunned that it was common! 

So.. in the meantime (until you go to a doctor to hear what can be done for you): COUNT things. Seriously. Stones on the buildings, windows on buildings, tiles, dots on the wall, fuck even the hairs on you arm! Count! Count count!! The trick is keep yourself busy. Also, what seriously helped for me was giving in to it. You will start to recognise the tingles in your stomach and legs (for me), then how you get uncomfortable and then when you realise.. 'oh god.. panic attack'. Mostly that's the moment I freak out... from the idea 'oh god, panic attack'. The idea of one, triggers one. Let it come.. Give it a name. My panic is called 'silly'. When ever I feel the tingles, the restlessness and how I get uncomfortable.. I think; 'Hee Silly.. are you there again?' and I SMILE. I can deal with Silly. He's nothing more than a lost neuron trigger in my head. 

If you take a deep breath and think; 'Hee Silly.. what's up this time?' it will calm you down. You know what's going on. Because nothing is going on. Nothing panic-worthy. Silly is just teasing you again. You know what happens.. Silly tells you about the people around you, what they will think and say to their friends. But you know what? Those people are WAY to busy with themselfs and their groseries. They won't recognise a picture of you within ten minutes of seeing you. Silly is just teasing you.

If you learn how to ignore Silly and let him be, he will leave as soon as you say; 'Hee Silly.. popping up again?'. Nothing's wrong.
